subject: [PATCH v3 0/2] memcg: reduce cacheline contention from lruvec stat

reviews.author: Andrew Morton
reviews.summary: The reviewer noted that even though the patch rearranges struct mem_cgroup_per_node to pair its read-mostly line with a cold line, it does not guarantee that every read-mostly line will be paired with a cold line due to SLAB_HWCACHE_ALIGN slab usage, which can align objects to 128-byte boundaries but still allow adjacent objects to share a cacheline pair.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks.  A local AI review pointed out a thing:

  One limitation worth mentioning in the [1/2] changelog: the slab
  uses SLAB_HWCACHE_ALIGN, which need not align each object to a
  128-byte boundary.  If an object starts 64 bytes into such a pair,
  its first line can still be paired with the end of the preceding
  object rather than its own cold line.  This isn't a correctness
  issue, and the measured Skylake improvement may well be real, but the
  layout doesn't guarantee that every read-mostly line pairs with a
  cold line.

2026-10-23.patch_summary: This patch reduces cacheline contention between lruvec stat updates and LRU lists by rearranging the layout of struct mem_cgroup_per_node to pair read-mostly lines with cold lines, and modifying folio and kmem stat updates to avoid going through the lruvec. This change improves performance on systems that use spatial prefetching, such as Intel CPUs. The patch includes two changes: one that reorders the fields in struct mem_cgroup_per_node, and another that modifies the stat update functions to skip using the lruvec. The results show a significant improvement in pages per second for threads faulting in and freeing memory in a single memcg.

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary: The author addressed Andrew's concern about the effectiveness of rearranging struct mem_cgroup_per_node, explaining that even when the read-mostly line isn't paired with a cold line, it's still not causing significant contention in practice. The author provided updated benchmarking results and suggested an alternative explanation for the uniform throughput across memcgs.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Andrew,

Thanks for taking a look at this series!

The AI review's commentary is correct but it doesn't seem to matter in
practice. In the cases where the read-mostly line isn't paired with
the cold line, it's paired with the line that holds the end of
lru_zone_size[] and the reclaim iterator, which are also rarely
written outside of reclaim so it doesn't see much contention. In my
benchmarking runs, the memcgs are freshly created and contain a mix of
both alignments. Before the changes in this series, the per-memcg
throughput was bimodal depending on the alignment, but afterwards, the
throughput is uniform across memcgs.

Here's an updated version of the "Fix this by moving the memcg_pn_cold
group..." paragraph in patch 1 that mentions this:

Fix this by moving the memcg_pn_cold group, which is only touched when
the memcg is reparented or freed, right after memcg_pn_read_mostly.
SLAB_HWCACHE_ALIGN only aligns objects to a cacheline, and the struct
is 576 bytes, so depending on where an object lands, its read-mostly
cacheline is now paired either with its cold cacheline or with the last
cacheline of the preceding object, which holds the end of
lru_zone_size[] and the reclaim iterator. Both are rarely written
outside of reclaim, so either way the read-mostly cacheline is no
longer paired with the LRU list heads.

Would you be able to swap it in or would you prefer that I send a v4?

Thanks,
Joanne

reviews.author: Andrew Morton
reviews.summary: Reviewer Andrew Morton acknowledged receipt and indicated that he will process the patchset, but did not provide any technical feedback or comments.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks.  I'll take care of this when I process the patchset.  Which
will be quite soon now we're all merged up.
